To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most efficient regulatory policy strategy for accelerating the production of oil is to design production increasing measures for accelerating cost firms, and to design cost increasing measures for accelerating production firms.

optimal regulatory policy in the oil industry can be designed by using a combination of production and cost increasing measures that are tailored to the level of operation and the type of inefficiencies exhibited by producer firms.

(a) the optimal policy effort for accelerating cost firms is to design production increasing measures; (b) the optimal policy for accelerating production firms is to design cost increasing measures; and (c) the optimal policy strategy is to design cost incentive policies for firms that have a high level of cost inefficiency and production incentive policies for firms having a high level of production inefficiency.

identifying the problems associated with the design of regulatory policy in the oil industry, and offering an alternative framework for resolving such problems.
the design of optimal strategies for the regulation of oil production.
identifying and measuring the inefficiencies in the oil industry and the policy instruments that should be adopted to eliminate such inefficiencies.

the optimal regulatory policy strategy is to design production increasing measures for accelerating the production of cost inefficient firms (accelerated cost firms), and cost increasing measures to accelerate the cost of production of production inefficient firms (accelerate production firms).

the optimal regulatory strategy for the oil industry is to adopt a policy of cost increasing measures to accelerate production firms and a policy of production increasing measures to accelerate cost firms.
the optimal regulatory policy strategies in the oil industry are to design cost increasing policy instruments for accelerating production and cost decreasing policy instruments for accelerating cost.
